- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underreacts to downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion in early periods; if recent 5-day avg is below 78.0, forecast should not exceed 79.5 unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; if last 3 days show high variance, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often fails to capture gradual upward drift; add 0.2–0.8% upward bias if sentiment > -0.10 and no recent spike.
